title: Exploring the adsorption behavior of heavy metals on AlZnO and AlZnO@g-C 3 N 4 : a comprehensive kinetic, isotherm, and mechanistic study
content: Developing sorbents that combine high affinity with clear mechanistic understanding is essential for the rational design of next-generation materials for heavy-metal remediation. In this work, Al-doped ZnO (AlZnO) and its carbon–nitride-modified composite (AlZnO@g-C3N4) were synthesized and systematically evaluated for the adsorption of Cd(ii), Cu(ii), and Mn(ii). A comprehensive structure–performance correlation was established by integrating detailed physicochemical characterization (XRD, FTIR, SEM, BET) with kinetic, isotherm, and thermodynamic modeling. Incorporation of g-g-C3N4 significantly increased BET surface area and pore volume and introduced carbon–nitride functionalities, resulting in higher pseudo-second-order rate constants, larger Langmuir monolayer capacities, and more negative calculated ΔG° values. Cd(ii) consistently exhibited the strongest affinity on both sorbents, followed by Cu(ii) and Mn(ii), a selectivity trend explained by differences in hydration enthalpy, HSAB character, coordination behavior, and diffusional accessibility. The adsorption trends are consistent with potential contributions from oxide oxygen groups, carbon–nitride nitrogen functionalities, and pH-dependent surface interactions. This work provides a structure–performance interpretation of adsorption on oxide–nitride hybrids and demonstrates the critical role of carbon–nitride functionalization in improving metal-ion affinity and adsorption energetics, offering valuable insight for the rational design of advanced sorbents.
